totals.tax_note: Explicitly a repair, not a new build or complete replacement. Under NYS Publication 862 this is taxable on the full billed amount including labour, materials, equipment and markup. No Form ST-124 applies.

cross_check.why: The rate card prices masonry per unit — per square foot, per linear foot, per stone. Those bands assume normal access and a mason working with a tender. This job has a small quantity of work and a large quantity of getting to it. So the two legitimate ways to price it disagree, and the tool surfaces the disagreement rather than silently picking the one it likes.

method_a.name: Unit price, off the rate card
method_a.note: Every line derived in Section 6. All-in per the card's Total Est. convention.

method_b.name: Day rate, off the card's quick reference
method_b.note: 6 on-site days — the same 6 the lift is modelled at in Section 7b — at the card's mason rate of $75–110/hr over 8-hour days, plus $590 materials. Solo working, so no tender rate applies. Siting and strike days are Dan's time too.

cross_check.gap: Unit pricing lands at $2,440. Day-rate pricing lands at $4,190–$5,870. The unit method is LOW by roughly $1,750–$3,430 — it does not merely differ from the day-rate method, it is under half of it at the top of the band.
cross_check.reading: This is not a rounding difference, it is the rate card telling on itself. Per-unit rates price PRODUCTION. On this job Dan is not mostly producing — he is positioning a machine, climbing, carrying stone one piece at a time, and repositioning. A small quantity in an awkward place costs day-rate money regardless of how few square feet it is.
cross_check.recommendation: Price this job on days, not units, and use the unit figure only as a floor. The rate card's own minimum-job clause ($350–600) exists for the same reason — it acknowledges that below a certain size, quantity stops predicting cost. This job is that case at a larger scale.
cross_check.instruction: Dan's call. The tool will not silently switch methods — it shows both and says which it would use.
cross_check.headline: Day rate. Not per square foot.

tax_lines.basis: Dan stated explicitly: 'It is a repair job. It's not a new build.' NYS Publication 862 classifies repair and partial replacement of masonry as taxable; new installation and COMPLETE replacement are capital improvements. No line here reaches complete replacement.
Follows the character of the work it serves.
Capital improvement certificates apply only to exempt work. Requesting one here would be wrong and would look like Dan does not know his own tax position.
Demolition to the roofline with the opening closed is arguably neither repair nor improvement. Genuinely unsettled — accountant question, flagged rather than answered.

THE AREA IS INVENTED. An assumed 11 ft perimeter over the top 4 ft. Nobody measured the chimney, and 'absolutely massive' suggests the assumption may be low. This is the single largest guess in the estimate and it is the first thing the site visit settles.

Dan could not establish the count from the ground and said so. The tool carries the uncertainty forward as an allowance of three units at mid-band ($230 each) rather than resolving it into a false number. Billed as performed; each additional unit is $120–350.

explanation: The chimney is out of service, so this is stabilisation, not restoration — the cost is in reaching the work, not in the work.
scope_sentence: Rake and repoint the failed joints in the upper section of the stone chimney, reset shifted units, and seal the top against water entry. Chimney remains out of service.

objections.objection: Why not just patch the crack from a ladder?
objections.response: Over twenty feet with stone that has already shifted, a ladder gives you one hand and no way to hold a unit while you bed it. The units come out and go back either way.
objections.grounded_in: Memo: 20+ ft, stones appear to have shifted

objections.objection: Can you use regular mortar? It is cheaper.
objections.response: Pre-1930 stone takes Type N or NHL lime. Portland is harder than the stone and spalls the face — you would be repairing the repair.

objections.objection: The chimney does not even work. Why spend anything?
objections.response: It is enclosed by the house. If the upper section keeps moving, what it comes down onto is roof and interior, not lawn.

validity: Holds 30 days. Stone and lime are the volatile inputs — the card flags materials up 8-14% since 2024.
next_steps: One site visit: measure path width at its narrowest, path length from the truck, height to the work, and ground condition.

One call to a rental yard with those numbers: weekly rate before day rate, stowed chassis width, platform capacity with a material rack, delivery and pickup quoted separately, and whether the damage waiver covers the property.
